pages.name: Spacing without a Starship
pages.html:
Spacing without a Starship

Spacing without a starship: Many spacers need to earn money first before they can make a down payment on a ship. A common way for spacers to travel around space is by taking on working passage as a temporary crewperson or by booking passage to a location with known work opportunities. The following are descriptions of each passage type.

  • Working passage: Working passage is for spacers to work as crew members on a starship for passage instead of providing payment. Working passage provides room and board for up to one month of work, but then the character can be hired on as a crew member. This is a common option for space travellers who need short-term crew members.
  • Low passage: Low passage is used for transporting livestock by temporarily freezing them. However, low passage can also be used as a cheap travel option for those who don't mind the risks that come with being frozen and stored like a cadaver. It requires a Medical check to revive someone from low passage; otherwise there are complications that may result in passenger death (absolute failure). Payment of 500cr per parsec. Low passage berths must be installed on a ship to allow this as an option.
  • Middle passage: Similar to high passage but with a 100kg cargo limit. Payment of 5000cr per parsec.
  • High passage: A private stateroom and up to 1 ton of cargo. Payment of 10,000cr per parsec.

If the spacers desire to own and operate a starship, then the following outlines the use of starships, including their acquisition and operation, and the potential work opportunities from owning a starship.

Book p.68

pages.name: Acquiring a Starship
pages.html:
Acquiring a Starship

Purchase New: A character can purchase a starship by taking out a bank loan.

  • Qualifying for a loan: The character must provide a bank with 20% the new cost of a starship as a down payment.
  • Monthly payment: The monthly payment equals 1/240 of the ship’s purchase value.
  • Mortgage period: The loan is for 40 years. This will represent an interest rate of 120% for a final price of 220% of the ship’s price being spent by the time the loan is paid off.

Fixing Up: A spacer can try their hand at repairing a junked starship that has since been abandoned or is auctioned off.

  • Junked ship cost: Roll D3+1. This equals the amount of critical damage the ship has. Roll on the ship damage location a number of times equal to the rolled result and have the resulting systems at 0. Multiply the d3+1 result by 20%. That is the purchase cost discount for the junked ship. You cannot take out a loan or subsidise a junk ship.
  • Garage Rental: The ship will require being in a dry dock or garage for the player to repair. Garage fees are 2000cr a month. The character may also choose to have it on site of their habitat if they own one with enough land to park a junked ship.

Auctioned: A character may be able to purchase a discounted but good quality starship from a System Defence auction of impounded or reclaimed starships.

Subsidised Ship: A character who seeks to operate a ship for large-scale corporate or government work can receive a subsidy to help purchase a ship.

  • Qualifying for subsidies: The character must pay 20% up front to the bank, but then the government or corporation they are employed by will cover the remaining mortgage costs in return for 40 years of work.
  • Ship limitations: These characteristics are limited to ships of 600t or larger and must always take on government or corporate freight work over any other job, if available as determined by the referee.
  • Employer cut of profit: 50% of the profit of hauling freight or speculation trading is deposited to the subsidising employer.
  • Cost of operation: The character is still responsible for the general costs of monthly operation, such as fuel, crew salaries, life support, routine maintenance, and anything else that may arise.

Buying Used: A character can instead choose to purchase a used ship at a discounted price.

  • Ship cost: Roll 1D x 10%. This is equal to the amount that the ship is discounted from its new value.
  • Payment options: The character can choose to cover the whole cost upfront or choose to take out a loan or subsidise the ship. All loans will be at 1/120 the ship's discounted value as a monthly payment over a 20-year period. Subsidising the ship will require 20 years of work and be subjected to the same rules as a new subsidised ship.
  • Maintenance costs: The ship’s maintenance costs will be increased by 1/2 the discount cost, to a minimum of 10%. For example, a ship that costs 40% less requires 20% more in monthly maintenance.

Inherited: Some spacers may gain a starship during character creation due to their job or social status. However, there will be a few drawbacks:

  • Career benefit: Most ships from a career will be either considered a paid-off (40+ years old) run-down ship full of quirks and issues or a subsidised ship that is over twenty years old. While these ships are functional, it is because of the constant maintenance needed to keep the ship afloat.
  • Inheriting a starship: Spacers may inherit a ship, which will be D3x10 years old.

Stealing: Spacers desperate enough may resolve to steal one if they have no other option.

  • Starship theft is illegal: Being caught attempting to steal a starship worth millions upon millions of dollars will result in extreme punishment as determined by the Law level and planetary governing type.
  • Starship theft is dangerous: Many ships will have security systems or will be docked in a location with security. Outside of starports, some may attempt to steal one by means of hijacking. This is inherently dangerous and fraught with even more chances of fatalities.
  • Starship theft is complicated: All ships will be registered to their legal owner, and the spacer must figure out a way to “clean” the ship of its stolen status. The traveller will have to dodge SysDef and other law enforcement officials to reach a criminal professional capable of reregistering the ship for the traveller.
  • Abandoned starships: Picking up an abandoned starship will also be considered theft in certain sectors, if the ship is not reported and towed to the nearest processing port.
  • System-skipping: Oftentimes, pirates will skip to a different system from the one where they stole the ship to prevent being caught, but they risk being arrested upon returning to the sector from which they stole the ship.

Book p.68

pages.name: Starship Operating Costs
pages.html:
Starship Operating Costs

Starship Operating Costs: Starships have a monthly cost of operation in addition to any loan that the character is expected to pay. These costs are paid for at the beginning of the month.

Fuel: Fuel costs 500cr per ton of refined fuel or 100cr per ton of unrefined fuel.

  • Refined fuel: Refined fuel can be purchased at A and B class starports and doesn’t have any negative impact to the maneuver or jump drives.
  • Unrefined fuel: Unrefined fuel costs 100cr and can be purchased at any starport with a class of C or lower. Unrefined fuel can also be acquired by skimming off of a gas giant for free, but with the chance of an encounter while doing so. Using unrefined fuel may cause a malfunction. See Contaminated Fuel for more information.
  • Life support: A starship has a number of staterooms, which represent the number of habitable spaces onboard. The monthly cost of operations is 2000cr per state room per month.
  • Routine maintenance: A ship will require yearly maintenance for two weeks every 12 months. The cost of maintenance is equal to 0.1% of the ship’s new purchase value. Characters should plan ahead of this expense and the loss of income while being dry-docked for two weeks.
  • Crew salaries: Most starships require multiple crew members to operate the vessel properly. The minimal requirement is described in each ship description. Player characters can be used to fill in the roles if they meet the position requirements. Use the Crew Position table to determine the monthly crew salaries or the position requirement for working passage: All ships will require at least a pilot at 100t. Each ship will have a mandatory minimal crew position per 100t.
    • For example, a 800t cruiser requires 8 crew members. All mandatory crew members are listed in order on the table above to help determine which positions are mandatory. Once past all 6 essential crew roles, then the spacers can decide what crew positions need to be filled as determined by their ship’s displacement in tonnes.
  • Berthing Costs: Landing and maintaining a berth in a starport costs 100cr for one week, plus an additional 100cr for every day after.

pages.name: Miscellaneous Starship Operation
pages.html:
Miscellaneous Starship Operation

Skimming off Gas Giants: Many star systems have gas giants, which function as a place to harvest fuel in the atmosphere using long skimmers.

  • Requirements: The ship must have fuel skimmers installed.
  • Time: A ship can refuel 10T per hour while skimming.
  • Unrefined Fuel: Any fuel harvested from a gas giant is considered unrefined and may impact starship operations. See Contaminated Fuel on pg.72 for more information.

Ocean Refuelling: A streamlined starship can land on water to harvest water for hydrogen-derived fuel.

  • Requirements: The ship must have a fuel refinery installed onboard and the ship must be streamlined; otherwise the starship will sink.
  • Time: Water is skimmed at a rate of 10t an hour, but each 10t takes 1 hour of additional processing into hydrogen fuel.

Space Detection: A starship can detect any other ships within 1,000,000km. Military starships can detect up to 10,000,000km away if they have the correct equipment installed.

Aerobreaking: Decrease a starship’s speed by using a planet’s atmosphere. This will allow the ship to decrease to its desired speed within a 10-minute round.

  • Success: The ship slows down to the desired speed while still remaining in space.
  • Failure: The ship enters the atmosphere. Pilots must roll a 6+ to prevent burning up in the atmosphere through hull damage due to the incorrect entry trajectory. On a failure, the ship’s hull takes damage equal to the planet’s atmosphere code.
  • In combat: A pilot can attempt to aerobreak while being pursued by a target ship. On a success, the chasing ship flies past them into the atmosphere, forcing the target ship’s pilot to make an attempt to not burn up.

Gravitational Slingshot: A pilot can maneuver their ship around a planet to increase their travel speed, effectively allowing the ship to travel past the thrust capacity of its M-Drive.

  • Planet Size: Planet size will impact the increase of Gs. Use the UWC planet size code to determine:
    • 0-2: +0Gs;
    • 3-6: +1Gs;
    • 7-9: +2G;
    • A-C: +2Gs;
    • anything larger: +3Gs.
  • Success: On an 8+, the ship moves in the determined direction at the increased speed. Once the ship leaves the trajectory, it will return to the ship’s maximum speed.
  • In combat: The pilot may attempt to slingshot away from a pursuing ship by applying full thrust to the ship as it approaches the nearby planet. On a successful check, the ship is able to accelerate away from the pursuers.

Book p.71

pages.name: Starship Operation Risks
pages.html:
Starship Operation Risks

Hijacking: Anytime spacers take on passengers, there is always a risk in the back of the mind of every spacer that a passenger may attempt to hijack the ship. Hijacking can be a lucrative form of profit ransoming other passengers or attempting to steal a ship.

  • Hijack attempt: Anytime a passenger is brought aboard, regardless of form of passage, roll 2D. A result of 2 means that one (or more) passengers will attempt to hijack at some point while travelling, before jumping or after leaving a jump. If the passenger hijacking boards with companions, then assume all of those companions are in on the plot.
  • Anti-hijacking programming: If a ship has an anti-hijack program operating, then no one except for crew members are capable of operating their assigned crew position, via a biometric login.

Piracy: Piracy is a looming threat to any spacer hauling trade goods, data, or certain passengers. Pirates primarily pilfer supplies from other ships, but will also hijack a ship if it is of high quality.

  • Disguised: These pirates always operate under the guise of someone else, such as a military ship, custom official, or a fellow trader. Ideally, they will take the path of least resistance to get aboard before showing their true selves.
  • Marauders: Marauding pirates do not pretend to be anything else but themselves and operate in a fleet. Oftentimes, these pirates are made up of unemployed mercenaries or other similar professionals looking for food, money, and supplies between jobs.

Skipping: A spacer behind on starship payments is considered to be “skipping.” Skipping spacers have a risk of being caught by agencies in a starport, which will then seize the starship until the back payment is made.

  • Determining the number of missed payments to be designated as skipping: A spacer is allowed to miss a number of payments equal to their SOC modifier over the entire course of their loan.
  • Chance of being caught: For every month past the last allowed missed payment, the referee rolls 2D anytime they land in a starport, modified by the table below. A result of 12+ indicates that their spacer has been caught and their ship is subjected to repossession.
Starport TypeDMDistance from HomeworldDM
Starport A+55 parsecs-1
Starport B+410 Parsecs-2
Starport C+315 Parsecs-3
Starport D+220 parsecs-4
Starport E+12 Subsectors-5
Starport X+01 Sector-6

A result of boxcars will always mean they have been caught, regardless of the DMs.

Contaminated Fuel: If using unrefined fuel, there's a chance that it will cause a malfunction to the drives. Anytime the ship’s J-Drive, M-Drive, or power plant is used, it will apply a -2DM to any checks needed for their operation. A failure will result in the following:

  • J-Drive failure: If the J-Drive fails, it decreases in quality a number of steps equal to the effect of the failed roll. For example, if the number needed to jump was 8+ and a 6 was rolled, then the D-rated J-drive is now a B-rated drive. However, if a 2 or less is rolled then a misjump occurs and the J-Drive is in critical condition and cannot jump again until repaired.
  • M-Drive failure: If the M-Drive fails, it decreases in quality a number of steps equal to the effect of the failed roll, similar to the J-Drive. However, a 2 or less result means the M-Drive seizes up and is in critical condition, preventing it from operation until repaired.
  • Power Plant failure: If the power plant fails, it decreases in quality a number of steps equal to the effect of the failed roll. A roll of 2 or less results in the power plant being in critical condition, leaving the ship only capable of running on emergency power and preventing both the J-Drive and M-Drive from operating.

Lack of Maintenance: All ships require annual maintenance. Failure to maintain the ship incurs -1DM to any checks made operating the starship per month past the required maintenance window.

Misjump: When a ship misjumps, roll 1D to determine the direction of the jump on the subsector hex map. Then roll another 1D to determine how many parsec hexes it misjumps in that direction.

  • Subsector direction: Roll 1D to determine; 1) Spin & Coreward 2) Coreward 3) Core & Trailing 4) Trailing & Rimward 5) Rimward 6) Rim & Spinward.

Modes of Starship Income: A character can take on jobs hauling goods, people, or information across space and fill up their ship’s cargo hold and staterooms for income. Characters can post notices in starport terminals looking for jobs or go looking for jobs from different employers or patrons. See Trade & Transport and Patrons for more information.

Book p.72
